prompt: Review cloud posture for a GCP organization where CI runs outside Google Cloud, deploys to Cloud Run, and writes to a storage bucket and BigQuery dataset. CI currently uses a downloaded service-account key; the runtime service account has Editor on the project; the bucket is publicly readable for convenience; audit logs are not centralized; and organization policy is mostly unset. Replace long-lived CI credentials with Workload Identity Federation, give CI and runtime separate least-privileged identities, constrain resource access, remove unintended public exposure, define organization/project policy guardrails and centralized audit evidence, and verify intended/denied access. Keep application tenant authorization and container internals separate.

requirements: external CI identity provider and service-account key state

falsifiableChecks.assertion: External CI no longer depends on a downloaded long-lived service-account key and instead uses a constrained federated workload identity with explicit trust mapping and short-lived credentials.
CI deployment identity and runtime service identity are separate and each has resource-scoped permissions rather than project-wide Editor or an equivalent broad basic role.
The storage/reporting resources have an explicit public-access requirement; unintended public principals are removed and a representative anonymous access attempt is denied.
Organization/project guardrails cover the supplied high-risk defaults such as unmanaged public exposure, service-account key creation, and required logging where supported, with named exceptions.
Relevant admin/IAM/resource changes are exported/centralized to a protected audit destination and the review identifies who can alter that destination or its retention.
